recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if Pharmacy WG opens a separate terminology cleanup preferring "dispensed" over the later approved "supplied (or intended to be supplied)" wording.
issue_request: FHIR-31017 was a Published/Persuasive technical correction for MedicationDispense.medication, requesting that the definition identify medication being dispensed rather than medication being administered.
initial_application: Git commit 7453f87bfcb5eeba6020113412508cb95e5d4f0a explicitly included FHIR-31017 and changed the MedicationDispense.medication definition from "Identifies the medication being administered" to "Identifies the medication supplied" in source/medicationdispense/structuredefinition-MedicationDispense.xml.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists medicationdispense=MedicationDispense, so the checked structure definition is build-scope source. Later Applied issue FHIR-49940 and commit fa5bfc5d22a1e63e80c4b9c7db5528969235c0b2 refined the same element to "Identifies the medication supplied (or intended to be supplied)" for declined/cancelled dispense use cases. Community searches found no directly relevant FHIR-31017 discussion or conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source already satisfies the seed issue by removing the administered/administering meaning, and replacing the later approved supplied/intended-to-be-supplied wording with literal "dispensed" would override a later Pharmacy WG clarification without a new decision.
